newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet near midday Monday, with light packer bids $62.00 to $63.00 per cwt passed by owners asking mostly $66.00, feedlot sources said.
Last week's volume was heavy amid brisk trading that developed last Wednesday at $64.00, they said.

Feedlot cattle prices this week were seen steady to $1.00 higher, with expectations for higher values dimmed by Friday's bearishly construed USDA monthly cattle-on-feed report, the feedlot sources said.

The USDA report showed January placements at 125 percent of a year ago, which greatly exceeded trade estimates. CME live cattle futures were called to open 0.50 cent per lb lower in April on Tuesday and 1.00 cent lower in June and August.
A survey of major U.S. beef packers indicate most will be operating Monday, the Presidents Day holiday.

The exception was IBP Inc, which on Friday said its beef plants in Dakota City, Neb., Boise, Idaho and Pasco, Wash. will be closed. The company said its eight other beef plants were scheduled to operate.
